Where each prepared patch stands with upstream, what it costs us to carry, and what
the whole set costs if upstream accepts none of it.

Every patch here is traceable to a directory under
`codetracer-specs/upstream-bugs/`, which holds the patch itself, the `PR.md` written
for an upstream audience, and a verification script with a meaningful exit status.

## Order and dependencies

| # | Branch on our fork | Applies without | Builds without | Standalone |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `pr/1-crypto-merkle-tree-lmdb-split` | anything | anything | yes |
| 2 | `pr/2-wasi-sdk-33` | anything | anything | yes |
| 3 | `pr/3-widen-before-shifting` | anything | anything | yes |
| 4 | `pr/4-execution-observation-hook` | anything | anything | yes |
| 5 | `pr/5-avm-wasm-module-split` | p1 | p2, p3 | **no** |

`applies without` names APPLY prerequisites — patches without which `git am` is
rejected. `builds without` names BUILD prerequisites — patches without which the tree
applies cleanly and then fails to compile. The two are different claims and were
established separately, by trying each combination rather than by grouping them.

* **Entry**: `codetracer-specs/upstream-bugs/aztec-merkle-tree-lmdb-split/`
* **Branch**: `pr/1-crypto-merkle-tree-lmdb-split` on `metacraft-labs/aztec-packages`

Largest of the five and the only one that moves paths: 35 files, 9 renames, 1 deletion. Renames are cheap to carry — upstream has no version of the new path to move under us — but expensive to rebase if upstream edits the old path, and the audit-scope document it updates is a file upstream also maintains.

## Total exposure if nothing is accepted

Measured against `233d8e0993` (2026-08-19) with `tools/measure_carry_exposure.py`, not estimated.

**Size.** 53 distinct files, +611 / −293. That is git's own diff between the base
and the base with all five patches applied — what the SET costs — and it is not the
same arithmetic as summing the five per-patch rows, which gives +613 / −295 over 80
hunks. The two differ because 3 file(s) are touched by more than one patch and one
patch's added line can be another's context. Both are stated so neither can be quoted
as the other. The 80 hunks are a property of the patch files, not of the endpoint diff.

| Category | Files | Changed lines |
| --- | --- | --- |
| c++ | 37 | 709 |
| cmake | 11 | 138 |
| other | 2 | 36 |
| shell | 3 | 21 |

**Conflict surface.** 6 file(s) are created by the series, 9 renamed and 1
deleted; those cost nothing to rebase, because upstream has no version of them to
move underneath us. **37 files are modified**, and those are the whole conflict
surface.

**Churn.** Over the twelve months before the base (`2025-08-19` .. `2026-08-19`), upstream made
**41.17 commits per month** touching a file this series modifies, and
**6.58 per month** touching the LINES it modifies. The second number is the one
that predicts a rebase conflict; the first is an upper bound on it.

The eight files whose carried lines upstream touched most, in that window:

| Commits on the carried lines | File |
| --- | --- |
| 16 | `barretenberg/cpp/src/barretenberg/vm2/simulation_helper.cpp` |
| 9 | `barretenberg/cpp/src/CMakeLists.txt` |
| 9 | `barretenberg/cpp/src/barretenberg/vm2/common/avm_io.hpp` |
| 5 | `barretenberg/cpp/cmake/arch.cmake` |
| 5 | `barretenberg/cpp/src/barretenberg/vm2/simulation/gadgets/execution.hpp` |
| 4 | `barretenberg/cpp/CMakeLists.txt` |
| 4 | `barretenberg/cpp/src/barretenberg/vm2/simulation/standalone/hybrid_execution.cpp` |
| 3 | `barretenberg/cpp/src/barretenberg/world_state/CMakeLists.txt` |

**Against the spike's estimate.** The spike said "roughly 80 lines of CMake plus
one function-level rebase risk in `hybrid_execution.cpp`". Measured, the CMake
side is **11 files and 138 changed lines**, not 80; and `hybrid_execution.cpp` is
**not** the top rebase risk: 4 upstream commits landed on its carried lines in
twelve months, against 16 for `simulation_helper.cpp`. The estimate named the
wrong file and understated the CMake side.

## Rebase harness

`just rebase-upstream-patches` fetches upstream and replays the set onto its tip,
reporting per patch whether it applies, is already present, or conflicts — and on
which files. It exits non-zero if any patch we still carry stops applying. CI runs it
weekly and on every change to the series, so the cost is a dated failure rather than
a discovery during an emergency.

Last recorded replay, onto `upstream/next` (127dec3ec9), 3 commit(s) past the base:

| --- | --- |
| `p1` | applies |
| `p2` | applies |
| `p3` | applies |
| `p4` | applies |
| `p5` | applies |

## Filing

Nothing in this repository files anything upstream, and no automation may. Each
patch has one script; a human runs it:

    submit/pr1-crypto-merkle-tree-lmdb-split.sh
    submit/pr2-wasi-sdk-33.sh
    submit/pr3-widen-before-shifting.sh
    submit/pr4-execution-observation-hook.sh
    submit/pr5-avm-wasm-module-split.sh

Each one checks that its branch still rebuilds byte for byte from its patch file,
runs the tracker search the entry requires (and stops if the search cannot run),
refuses to open a second pull request for a branch that already has one, and records
the URL back into `carry/series.json`, the entry's `PR.md` and this ledger. Add
`--dry-run` to see exactly what would be sent without sending it.

The fifth refuses to run until the first three have been filed, because it stacks on
them and its body names their pull request numbers.
